places.name: Brackenport
places.description: Tarred rope, wet cobblestones, and bread cooling on a windowsill. Every expedition begins at the harbor.
lines: The old lights have gone quiet. Three beacons, three shores. We used to navigate by their song.
Take my folding skiff. It opens itself when your boots meet the water. The roads will carry you inland.
Wake the lights at Mosswatch, Frostspire, and the Sunken Bell. Then climb to the observatory.

places.name: Mosswatch
places.description: Roots hold this watchtower together. Somewhere inside, a little green flame is still waiting.
lines: A lantern is only a promise someone has kept.
The western light answers. Across the trees, windows begin to glow.

places.name: Hollowmere
places.description: Wooden houses stand above the marsh on stilts. Their reflections seem to have an extra floor.
lines: The lake east of here was not always a lake. The hill simply opened one night.
I have been fishing here for sixty years. I have never caught the same kind of fish twice.

places.name: The Glass Eye
places.description: A perfectly still lake fills the mouth of an extinct volcano. The stars appear here before they appear overhead.
places.person: A line in your field journal
lines: Nothing stirs. Even the skiff leaves no wake.
You draw the circle carefully. Somehow it comes out as an eye.

places.name: Northgate
places.description: A narrow pass opens onto a cluster of steep roofs. Smoke hangs low against the snow.
lines: The high peaks are impassable. Follow the pale road through the pass.
Frostspire is across the eastern strait. Best sail before the fog rolls in.

places.name: Frostspire
places.description: A tower of black stone rises from a white ridge. Snow falls upward around its crown.
lines: I kept a place for you by the fire. I knew you would arrive.
The northern light answers. For a moment, every snowflake is a tiny star.

places.name: Wayfarer's Rest
places.description: A crooked inn leans into the sea wind. Travelers have scratched a hundred maps into its tables.
lines: Our beds are dry, our soup is hot, and our directions are mostly correct.
Three old lights. One observatory. That is a story with an ending, if you keep walking.

places.name: The Empty Court
places.description: The walls have fallen, but the garden still blooms. Someone tends it. No one has seen them.
lines: WE BUILT OUR WALLS TO KEEP THE WORLD OUT.
The inscription ends there. A small flower grows through the final letter.

places.name: The Observatory
places.description: A brass telescope points at a dark patch of sky. Its three empty lenses are shaped like lantern flames.
lines: When the three beacons burn, the old sky will find its way home.
You do not need to conquer a world to leave it brighter.

places.name: Cedarhaven
places.tag: The town that smells of rain
places.description: Tall cedars shelter a little harbor. Paper lanterns carry the names of ships that never came home.
lines: The desert begins where the river forgets its name. Follow it south.
If you hear a bell beneath the dunes, you are getting close.

places.name: The Sunken Bell
places.description: Only the belfry remains above the sand. A cool wind rises from its buried doorway.
lines: We buried the city. We could not bury its song.
The eastern light answers. Somewhere beneath your feet, a bell rings once.

places.name: Lastwater
places.tag: Shade at the end of the road
places.description: A ring of palms surrounds a spring so clear it looks empty. The tea is much stronger than it looks.
lines: Everyone asks how far to the next town. Nobody asks how long to the next good cup of tea.
You may refill your flask. The spring belongs to whoever is thirsty.

places.name: The Sleeping Choir
places.tag: An island humming in its sleep
places.description: Seven stones lean toward the sea. At low tide, the water between them begins to hum.
places.person: A line in your field journal
lines: You stay for a while. There is no particular reason to leave.
One of the stones is warm to the touch.

places.name: The Paper Saint
places.tag: The ship that sailed too far
places.description: A shipwreck rests on the island like a beached cathedral. Flowers grow from the captain's desk.
lines: DAY 114. The charts end here.
DAY 115. We have decided to continue.
